digest.component_or_area: MCP error handling and CLI-MCP interface alignment
propositions: MCP tool failures currently surface as unstructured prose or ad-hoc partial shapes, while the CLI emits a structured error_envelope discriminator with machine codes; MCP must emit the same vocabulary-controlled codes on every failure path

The error codes are scattered across CLI emitter sites without a centralized registry; a single error_code_for(exc) classifier and KNOWN_ERROR_CODES frozenset must be the single source of truth, importable by library, CLI, and MCP

The library currently does not expose a machine error code uniformly (RebarError/ConcurrencyError have no .error attribute), blocking a three-way cross-interface test; the classifier must be re-exported as rebar.error_code_for

TicketNotFoundError must be a new ReadError subclass raised only at the two genuine not-found sites (reads.py:310/313) so error_code_for classifies by isinstance, not message substring, making the code message-independent per AC4

MCP soft errors in _mcp_reads.py (explain_criterion) and _mcp_llm.py currently return divergent ad-hoc shapes; they must be migrated to emit vocabulary codes (criterion_unknown_id/malformed_registry/missing_file; llm_unavailable) while preserving existing agent-branching fields (kind, resolution_class, retryable, diagnostic)

The error_envelope schema must relax input from required to optional to accommodate target-less failures (gate refusals), while CLI envelopes continue passing input unchanged, and MCP failure surface must be documented in docs/output-schemas.md with a pointer in docs/mcp-reference.md
